stories.title: Brent ~$107.35 as Hormuz traffic collapses and Saudi pipeline stays dark

facts.text: Reuters (1002 GMT Tue): Brent +$1.67 / +1.58% to $107.35/bbl; WTI +$2.14 / +2.11% to $103.53 — material lift vs morning’s ~$107.05 / ~$102.92 (04:06 GMT).
Kpler via Reuters: commodity vessel traffic through Hormuz fell to four on Monday (from 10 Sunday) — route previously carried ~1/5 of global oil supply.
Saudi East-West pipeline still offline after Friday attacks; traders say exportable crude at Yanbu could run out within days; Goldman repair notes range “very soon” to ~eight weeks.
Oman Maritime Security Centre: Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia under tow to an Omani port after an engine-room fire following an attack.
Separately: Reuters calc — half of Russia’s six top diesel-producing refineries cut or halted September output after drone damage.

stories.whyItMatters: Fresh midday tape and Hormuz throughput data tighten the supply scare morning already flagged — the main inflation/Fed-week driver into Wednesday.

stories.title: Fed expected to hike Wednesday — first in three years under Warsh

facts.text: AP via WTOP: Fed widely expected to lift the short-term rate Wednesday for the first time in three years to fight sticky inflation — at odds with Trump’s preference for a cut.
Current funds rate cited ~3.6%; Chair Kevin Warsh gives fewer forward signals than predecessors; Jackson Hole speech two weeks ago argued the 2% inflation goal is not yet met.
As recently as March the Fed had forecast one cut this year; AP frames Iran-war oil spikes plus AI data-center spending as keeping inflation above target longer.
Morning desk already had CME FedWatch ~90% for a 25 bp hike; afternoon AP package is the clear Wed-decision framing.

stories.whyItMatters: Lunch-time packaging of the Wednesday decision against oil and AI-capex inflation — the next hard catalyst after Monday’s chip rout.

stories.title: Investors probe AI capex after weekend safety-slowdown calls

facts.text: Reuters (15 Sep): investors nervous about any AI spending slowdown after Amodei/Altman/Musk weekend safety warnings — but several PMs say they need cancelled orders/deals, not talk.
BofA Global Research via Reuters: hyperscalers (MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META/ORCL) expected ~$795B capex in 2026 and nearly $1.08T in 2027.
Monday SOX still ~+60% YTD despite the selloff; picks-and-shovels hit harder than hyperscalers on any capability-pace pause, per Arena Private Wealth’s Kratz.
Trump on Monday called AI safety threats “a hoax” and downplayed regulation — another input into the same tape.

stories.whyItMatters: Afternoon follow to morning’s chip rout: the debate shifts from weekend rhetoric to whether capex actually slips into Fed week.

stories.title: Apple ships iOS 27 / macOS 27 with Siri AI

facts.text: Apple Newsroom: major platform updates rolling out today across iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 and other Apple platforms.
Headline feature: Siri AI — next-gen Apple Intelligence Siri with personal context, onscreen awareness, and world knowledge; dedicated Siri app syncs chat history via iCloud.
Also shipping: stronger parental controls plus Apple Intelligence upgrades in Photos (Spatial Reframing, Extend, Clean Up) and Image Playground.
HN discussion spiked overnight on the same Newsroom release (702 comments in the broader overnight digests).

stories.whyItMatters: Biggest consumer-software ship of the day — Siri AI is Apple’s answer to the same AI cycle hammering chip stocks this week.
